exposure: Time since tranexamic acid infusion (3, 7, 15, 30 minutes, then every 30 minutes up to 5 hours)
outcome: Rotational thromboelastometry parameters (EXTEM maximum clot firmness, EXTEM maximum clot lysis)
Transfusion of packed red blood cells
cohort: 20 women aged 18 to 50 years, ≥23 weeks of gestation undergoing cesarean delivery with at least 1 major (placenta previa, suspected placenta accreta spectrum, or active bleeding) or 2 minor (≥2 previous cesarean deliveries, previous postpartum hemorrhage, chorioamnionitis, polyhydramnios, macrosomia, obesity, or suspected placental abruption) risk factors for postpartum hemorrhage
finding: Following a standard 1g intravenous dose of tranexamic acid during cesarean delivery in patients at high risk of hemorrhage, a plasma concentration of ≥10 μg/mL, which is known to inhibit 80% of fibrinolysis, was sustained for at least 60 minutes, and plasma tranexamic acid levels correlated inversely with body mass index.
